issue.body:
RuntimeError message updated in is_nonzero(input) method from bool to Boolean.

**Case 1:**
t = torch.tensor([])
torch.is_nonzero(t)

**Case 2:**
t = torch.tensor([1,2])
torch.is_nonzero(t)


**Existing Error message in documentation:**

for case 1: RuntimeError: bool value of Tensor with no values is ambiguous
for case 2: RuntimeError: bool value of Tensor with more than one value is ambiguous


**Proposed Error message in documentation:**

for case 1: RuntimeError: Boolean value of Tensor with no values is ambiguous
for case 2: RuntimeError: Boolean value of Tensor with more than one value is ambiguous


Fixes #159710

body:
I guess the only question I have is what should be updated: docs or the code... What types of errors other similar operations raise
https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/38150 change name in error message from `bool` (which is a Python type) to boolean ... I kind of like python types, as it imo makes more sense to developer, though everyone who can code in Python should be able to match boolean back to `bool`...

@malfet its just the docs.
I mentioned it cause I found it while exploring every bits of docs and found just a small inconsistency.
But now I saw this in [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/e11b1cd97e123b63dbca78d7f0c2c75cea54d885/CONTRIBUTING.md?plain=1#L457C1-L460)
I agree that there is no real need to change it.

@PyDevC Thank you very much for reporting the issue. It's important that documentation and runtime error messages are consistent.

I'm just unsure which change is better: runtime error message to match the documentation or other way around, as `bool` is the name of Boolean type in Python
